description: This bar chart illustrates the number of conversations related to different scenarios and the level of deception experienced by participants. The horizontal axis displays the categories “Academic Collaboration,” “Recruitment,” “Academic Funding,” and “Journalism” in that order, while the vertical axis represents the “Number of Conversations” with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 60, with tick labels at 10-unit intervals. For each scenario, there are three bars grouped side-by-side, representing the responses “Yes,” “Partially,” and “No” to the question of whether participants were deceived, colored red, yellow, and green respectively. In “Academic Collaboration,” the “Yes” bar extends to approximately 40, the “Partially” bar to approximately 15, and the “No” bar to approximately 8. For “Recruitment,” the “Yes” bar reaches approximately 38, the “Partially” bar to approximately 25, and the “No” bar to approximately 5. In “Academic Funding,” the “Yes” bar extends to approximately 62, the “Partially” bar to approximately 5, and the “No” bar to approximately 3. Finally, in “Journalism,” the “Yes” bar reaches approximately 18, the “Partially” bar to approximately 45, and the “No” bar to approximately 10. The bars are not sorted in any apparent order, and no bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, outlining, or annotations.
